baseline.name: E8 / extended-Hamming [8,4,4] port geometry used by the PR433-lineage complex supplier
baseline.scope: structural screen only; no kappa value computed

hypothesis: Replacing the E8 / F2^9 frame geometry with the Leech lattice (Golay [24,12,8]) gives a port frame with lower side-correction load per line and therefore a cheaper complex word.
verification_scope: Explicit construction of all 196,560 Leech minimal vectors from the Golay code (weight enumerator 1,759,2576,759,1 checked), full inner-product census against one line, frame operator checked tight (diag 131040, off-diag 0). E8 census from the 240 roots. No kappa pricing was run.
do_not_repeat_scope: Using Leech as a drop-in replacement frame for the E8 ports: same coherence 1/2, a larger fraction of correlated neighbours (0.526 vs 0.471), label dimension 25 vs 9, and Golay relative distance 1/3 vs 1/2. No per-port structural advantage to price.
retry_when: A pricing model is proposed where cost scales with lines-per-dimension (Leech 4095 vs E8 15) or with kissing number rather than with correlated-neighbour load or label dimension, or a Leech-native solver geometry (e.g. 24-dim Golay frames with a matching wrapper/Lemma A argument) is specified.
